newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ANZ's NZ commodity index falls in April.
newsitem.headline: ANZ's NZ commodity index falls in April.

text.p: The average New Zealand dollar price of New Zealand's commodity exports fell 1.7 percent in April following a 0.2 percent fall in March, ANZ Bank said on Wednesday.
ANZ said its commodity price index showed the corresponding average world price of New Zealand's commodity exports fell by 2.5 percent in April following a 0.8 percent rise in March.
The NZ dollar price index eased slightly to 98.1 from 99.8 in March and the world price index fell to 122.8 from 126.
On an annual basis, the New Zealand index fell by 10.1 percent and the world price index fell by 6.5 percent.

The drop in the world price index was the first significant fall since mid-1996, ANZ said. It was precipitated by weaker prices for a broad range of commodities including wool, lamb, aluminium, diary products excluding cheese, and forestry products excluding logs.

The impact on the New Zealand dollar index was partially offset by a depreciation in the the unit against the U.S. dollar and sterling. An improvement in skin, cheese, log and kiwifruit prices occurred over the month, the bank added.
